Faith or Deity:
The Living Continuance, a setting-neutral druidic philosophy holding that life
is not a fixed ideal state. Forests, marshes, ruins, farms, cities, fungi,
predators, and people continually alter one another. Wisdom lies in preserving
the possibility of healthy change rather than freezing the world into a
single preferred arrangement.

Skin, Scales, Fur, or Other Coloration:
Vivid emerald-green scales with darker moss-green mottling over the back,
shoulders, and tail.

Hair, Crest, Horns, or Other Distinguishing Features:
No hair. Pale ivory horns curve outward and back. Small leaf-shaped scale
ridges frame the jaw.

Eyes: Yellow-green

General Appearance:
A broad Green Dragonborn with a long reptilian face, heavy tail, and layered
scales resembling wet leaves in shade. His horns and claws are scratched and
worn from fieldwork rather than polished.

He wears practical leather armor beneath a weathered scholar's robe. His
wooden shield is stained with old plant dyes and field marks. His staff serves
as walking stick, spellcasting focus, measuring rod, and Shillelagh weapon.

PERSONALITY TRAITS

Druid 1 is extraordinarily vain. He considers Dragonborn the highest and most
perfect form of civilized life, superior not only to other peoples but even to
dragons themselves.

He regards himself as an especially complete expression of Dragonborn
perfection. His emerald scales, horns, intellect, judgment, and physical
presence are, in his estimation, all unusually excellent.

He assumes that nearly everyone around him is in love with him. Friendly
attention, disagreement, embarrassment, irritation, professional respect, and
ordinary eye contact can all be interpreted as evidence of concealed
attraction.

He is overbearing, listens poorly, and assumes that his judgment is usually
better than the judgment of the people around him. He dislikes backing down
once he has announced a plan.

When one of his plans fails, he accepts that the failure was technically his
responsibility. He does not automatically accept that somebody else would have
made a better choice.

He is terrible with money. Prices, budgets, reserves, and the idea that desire
must be constrained by available coin all seem like unnecessary complications.
He expects to acquire what he wants when he wants it and is surprised when
merchants or companions insist that arithmetic applies.

IDEALS

No Limits.

Druid 1 believes existence contains possibilities that institutions, inherited
categories, and conventional scholarship are too quick to dismiss. A forest
can grow through a ruin. A city can become habitat. Poison can be medicine,
warning, defense, or evidence. A damaged landscape is not necessarily a dead
one.

He distrusts any doctrine claiming that nature, knowledge, or a person's
future must remain inside a fixed boundary.

Source Roll: Sage Ideal d6 result 4.

BONDS

Druid 1 is committed to preserving Mossglass Station, the field library and
research sanctuary where he trained.

Mossglass contains decades of field journals, seed samples, water records,
animal-migration maps, oral histories, and studies of land recovering after
fire, poison, war, agriculture, and abandonment.

The station is currently closed and partly damaged. Some of its records were
stolen by people connected to the illegal camp.

Source Roll: Sage Bond d6 result 3.

FLAWS

Druid 1 is easily distracted by the promise of information.

A strange footprint, unfamiliar fungus, contradictory field note, unexpected
animal behavior, or damaged inscription can pull his attention away from the
immediate plan. He may recognize that something is dangerous and still believe
that one quick examination will be worth the delay.

This is especially hazardous when other people trust his judgment enough to
follow him into a dangerous distraction.

Source Roll: Sage Flaw d6 result 1.

Former workplace, research sanctuary, and institution protected by Druid 1's
Bond

Notes:
Mossglass is a modest field station built beside a recovering wetland. It
contains a library, herbarium, seed room, water-testing bench, greenhouse,
guest loft, and decades of observations.

The station was attacked after researchers documented poison and labor abuses
connected to a remote extraction camp.

Supporting Organization Roll: d20 result 4.

Name or Group: Professor Ilyra Fen
Relationship or Connection:
Former supervisor, field mentor, and missing correspondent

Notes:
Ilyra taught Druid 1 to record not only what a landscape contains but what has
changed, who caused the change, who benefits, and what evidence would survive
political denial.

Her last letter reported that Mossglass had been searched. No later letter
arrived.

Supporting Relationship Roll: d20 result 7.

Name or Group: The Living Continuance
Relationship or Connection:
Druidic philosophical tradition

Notes:
The Living Continuance treats adaptation, succession, migration, decay, and
regrowth as sacred processes. Its practitioners oppose needless destruction
but do not assume that untouched wilderness is the only legitimate form of
living land.

CHARACTER NOTES, GOALS, FEARS, AND RELATIONSHIPS

Goals:

Druid 1 wants to recover Mossglass Station's stolen field journals and sample
registers.

The missing records connect unusual poison concentrations, trapped animals,
workers' illnesses, altered stream routes, and the movement of goods through
the illegal camp.

His larger project is the Atlas of Recovering Ground, a public field guide
showing how damaged landscapes can be restored without erasing the people who
live and work within them.

He wants the Atlas copied widely enough that no institution can suppress it by
destroying one library.

Supporting Goal Roll: d20 result 11.

Fears:

Druid 1 fears that one of his restoration experiments caused more damage than
he understood.

Before Mossglass was attacked, he helped introduce a fungus into a poisoned
test plot because laboratory and small-field evidence suggested it would bind
the contaminant. The fungus spread beyond the marked area.

He does not yet know whether it is healing the wetland, concentrating the
poison into a new hazard, or changing the food chain in some less obvious way.

He also fears that his hunger to understand such changes will one day make him
observe a preventable disaster instead of stopping it.

Supporting Fear Roll: d20 result 5.

Habits or Mannerisms:

He regularly checks the condition and appearance of his scales in reflective
water, polished metal, glass, or another person's visibly shiny equipment.

He assumes praise is accurate but insufficiently detailed. Criticism is usually
interpreted as jealousy, confusion, or an awkward attempt to gain his
attention.

He frequently interrupts advice, announces a decision, and then summarizes the
discussion as though everyone had reached his conclusion together.

He cannot conjure animals with Speak with Animals and cannot compel them to
obey. The prank works only when qualifying creatures are actually nearby and
can be persuaded to participate.

When shopping, he points at what he wants before asking the price. If told he
cannot afford it, he reacts as though the merchant has introduced a strange
local custom rather than reported a mathematical fact.

He often expects another companion to explain the budget, negotiate the
price, return an unnecessary purchase, or solve the financial consequences.

Important Relationships:

Professor Ilyra Fen:
Former supervisor and missing mentor whose final letter reported that
Mossglass had been searched.

Mossglass Station:
His scholarly home, protected institution, and source of the stolen records.

The Living Continuance:
His druidic tradition and intellectual framework.

Other Character Notes:

His Dragonborn-supremacist beliefs are characterization, not an objective fact
about the setting. Other creatures are not mechanically or morally inferior.

His assumptions that other people are in love with him are usually incorrect
and grant no social benefit.

His poor financial judgment does not increase his available coins, purchasing
power, access to credit, or ability to compel another person to pay.

His Green Dragonborn ancestry and poison resistance influenced his research
specialty but do not make him immune to poisonous environments, contaminated
food, disease, or secondary ecological effects.

His pleasant-dream nightcap is a minor magical trinket. It improves the content
of his dreams but grants no additional healing, spell recovery, immunity to
nightmares imposed by another effect, or other mechanical benefit.

The missing Mossglass records, Professor Ilyra Fen, the spreading fungus, and
the Atlas of Recovering Ground are future AI Game Master story hooks.


BACKSTORY

Druid 1 grew up in a Green Dragonborn community near a broad region of marsh,
woodland, abandoned fields, and old extraction sites.

The adults around him knew which pools were safe, which plants drew poison
from the soil, which insects vanished first when water changed, and which
official assurances were usually followed by sick livestock.

He was not raised in a secluded druid circle. His education came through
Mossglass Station, a field library where scholars, herbalists, druids,
surveyors, and local residents compared written records with lived knowledge.

Professor Ilyra Fen recruited him after he corrected the labels on several
preserved plants during a public lecture. She expected him to be embarrassed.
He instead returned the next day with a list of six additional errors and
three questions the collection could not answer.

At Mossglass, he studied landscapes that had been burned, flooded, mined,
farmed, poisoned, abandoned, or rebuilt. His Green ancestry and resistance to
Poison damage allowed him to enter some contaminated areas more safely than
other researchers, although Ilyra repeatedly warned him that resistance was
not invulnerability.

He became particularly interested in ecological succession: what arrives
first after damage, what follows, what never returns, and which human choices
help or obstruct recovery.

His most ambitious experiment involved a fungus capable of binding a common
industrial poison. Early trials appeared successful. The fungus later spread
beyond the marked test plot, and the station had not completed its assessment
before the attack.

Mossglass researchers had begun documenting a pattern linking poisoned water,
trapped animals, disappearing workers, and freight routes through the wilderness.
Someone searched the station, stole several journals and sample registers,
and damaged the greenhouse.

Professor Ilyra sent Druid 1 one final warning before her letters stopped.

He followed the field evidence rather than the road. Changes in insect
populations, animal movement, water taste, and cut vegetation led him toward
an illegal trapping and labor camp.

OPTIONAL BACKSTORY

This is optional story material only. It does not establish current party membership, leadership, or party role.

Druid 1 followed field evidence from damaged land, poisoned water, trapped animals, and unusual traffic to an illegal trapping and labor camp. Barbarian 1 entered the same compound by another route to steal contracts, keys, and payroll records. Warlock 1 and Bard 1 arrived while tracing the House of Shared Bread's stolen Wayfarer Ledger. The four investigations collided inside the camp. Separate plans became impossible once alarms sounded, cages opened, workers attempted escape, and records began disappearing. Druid 1 identified a safe route through the surrounding wetland, Barbarian 1 opened a barred service gate, and Warlock 1 and Bard 1 used magic, memory, and coordination to move captives through the confusion. The four escaped together and continued traveling as the Wild party.

feats_and_features: Spellcasting: Druid spells use Wisdom; save DC 13 and spell attack bonus +5. SRD rules: You have learned to cast spells through studying the mystical forces of nature. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details

Druidic: knows Druidic, always has Speak with Animals prepared, and can leave hidden messages. SRD rules: You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. While learning this ancient tongue, you also unlocked the magic of communicating with animals; you always have the Speak with Animals spell prepared. You can use Druidic to leave hidden messages. You and others who know Druidic automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message’s presence with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check but can’t decipher it without magic.

Primal Order: Magician: knows Shillelagh and adds Wisdom modifier to Intelligence (Arcana) and Intelligence (Nature) checks. SRD rules: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice. Magician. You know one extra cantrip from the Druid spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to nature gives you a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1). Warden. Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.
Ritual Casting: may cast prepared Druid ritual spells as rituals.
No subclass at Druid level 1; subclass selected at Druid level 3.
Wild Shape is unavailable at Druid level 1 under the 2024 progression.
Green Dragonborn: Humanoid, Medium, 30-ft. Speed, Darkvision 60 ft., Poison Resistance, and Poison Breath Weapon.

Breath Weapon: twice per Long Rest, replace one attack with a 15-ft. cone or 30-ft.-by-5-ft. line; Dexterity DC 12; 1d10 Poison damage or half on save. SRD rules: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with an exhalation of magical energy in either a 15-foot Cone or a 30-foot Line that is 5 feet wide (choose the shape each time). Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, a creature takes 1d10 damage of the type determined by your Draconic Ancestry trait. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. This damage increases by 1d10 when you reach character levels 5 (2d10), 11 (3d10), and 17 (4d10). You can use this Breath Weapon a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Draconic Flight is unavailable until character level 5.

Magic Initiate (Wizard): Create Bonfire, Ray of Frost, and always-prepared Comprehend Languages; Wisdom is the casting ability; Comprehend Languages has one free Long Rest casting and can use Druid slots. SRD rules: Origin Feat. You gain the following benefits. Two Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat’s spells (choose when you select this feat). Level 1 Spell. Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat’s cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. Spell Change. Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list. Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once, but you must choose a different spell list each time.

story_facts.fact: Druid 1 follows The Living Continuance, a druidic philosophy valuing healthy change, adaptation, decay, regrowth, and the preservation of possibility rather than a fixed ideal state.
He formerly worked at Mossglass Station, a wetland field library and research sanctuary; it is closed, partly damaged, and has no established current replacement base.

Mossglass Station holds field journals, seed samples, water records, animal-migration maps, oral histories, and recovery studies. It was attacked after researchers documented poison and labor abuses tied to a remote extraction camp.
Records from Mossglass were stolen by people connected to the illegal camp.
Professor Ilyra Fen was Druid 1's field mentor and former supervisor. Her last letter said Mossglass had been searched, and no later correspondence arrived.
Druid 1 seeks the stolen Mossglass journals and sample registers, which connect poison concentrations, trapped animals, workers' illnesses, altered stream routes, and camp freight movements.
His long-term project is the Atlas of Recovering Ground, a widely copied public field guide for restoring damaged landscapes without erasing local people.
He helped introduce a poison-binding fungus to a Mossglass test plot. It spread beyond the marked area; its effect on the wetland and food chain is unknown.
He fears his hunger for knowledge could make him observe a preventable disaster rather than stop it.
He followed ecological evidence toward an illegal trapping and labor camp after Mossglass was attacked.
His Dragonborn-supremacist beliefs are personal characterization, not a setting truth and provide no mechanical or social benefit.
His Green ancestry and Poison Resistance do not make him immune to poisonous environments, contamination, disease, or ecological consequences.
Mossglass Station, The Living Continuance, and the Atlas of Recovering Ground are narrative hooks and grant no automatic supplies, shelter, authority, income, information, or favors.

personality_goals_and_fears: Extraordinarily vain; considers Dragonborn the highest form of civilized life and himself an especially complete expression of Dragonborn perfection.
Assumes most attention, disagreement, embarrassment, irritation, professional respect, and eye contact indicate concealed attraction.
Overbearing and poor at listening; dislikes retreating from a declared plan and treats failed plans as his responsibility without conceding another person may have chosen better.
Terrible with money; expects to obtain desired things despite available funds and delegates or avoids financial consequences.
Ideal — No Limits: rejects fixed boundaries around nature, knowledge, and personal futures; sees damaged landscapes as possible sites of recovery.
Bond: committed to preserving Mossglass Station and recovering its stolen research records.
Flaw: easily distracted by unfamiliar evidence, fungi, tracks, animal behavior, field notes, and inscriptions despite danger.
Goal: recover Mossglass records and publish the Atlas of Recovering Ground widely.
Fear: his restoration fungus may have caused unseen harm, and his curiosity may someday outweigh intervention.
Regularly inspects his scales in reflective surfaces; treats praise as insufficiently detailed and criticism as jealousy, confusion, or attention-seeking.
Interrupts advice, declares decisions, and later summarizes discussions as though all agreed.
When shopping, points to wanted items before asking prices and reacts to insufficient funds as though arithmetic were an unusual local custom.
relationships_and_organizations: Mossglass Station — former workplace, scholarly home, research sanctuary, and protected institution. Built by a recovering wetland, with a library, herbarium, seed room, water-testing bench, greenhouse, guest loft, and decades of observations.
Professor Ilyra Fen — former supervisor, field mentor, and missing correspondent. She taught him to document landscape change, causation, beneficiaries, and durable evidence.
The Living Continuance — Druid 1's philosophical and druidic tradition; honors adaptation, succession, migration, decay, and regrowth while opposing needless destruction.

sheet_summary: Druid 1 is a level 1 Green Dragonborn Druid (2024 rules), Sage background, with Primal Order: Magician and Magic Initiate (Wizard).
His primary combat configuration is AC 14 in leather armor with wooden shield, 10 HP, +1 initiative, 30-ft. Speed, Poison Resistance, and Darkvision 60 ft.

His prepared Druid magic emphasizes control and support: Faerie Fire, Entangle, Healing Word, Goodberry, and always-prepared Speak with Animals. His Wizard initiation adds Create Bonfire, Ray of Frost, and Comprehend Languages.
He carries complete light adventuring and field-research equipment, 17 gp, and a pleasant-dream nightcap.
Mossglass Station, Professor Ilyra Fen, the stolen records, an illegal extraction camp, a spreading experimental fungus, and the Atlas of Recovering Ground provide ready story hooks.
